dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Owen. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, um, I'm not sure if I have the right department. Basically I need animal control, or whoever handles a dog that's out in the weather.
Okay. Let me make sure I understand. Is this a dog that you can see right now?

Yeah. So basically there's a dog tied up outside a house near where I'm parked, and it's raining pretty hard, like the soaker that's hitting today, and it's cold. It's been out here at least the last forty minutes.
All right. And can you tell me what the dog looks like? Size, color, that kind of thing.

Sure. It's a mid-size dog, maybe forty, fifty pounds. Kind of a brown and tan, like a shepherd mix, I think. Short coat. So it's not like a husky or anything built for this. It's basically soaked and kind of shaking.
Okay, brown and tan, medium size, short coat. Is there any kind of shelter? A doghouse, a porch, anything over it?
Not that I can see. There's a little overhang by the door but the rope's too short to reach it. It's basically just standing in the yard by a post.
I see. And do you have the address there? I'll need the location to pass along.

Um, I'd rather not say the house number, I'm kind of on a work call break and I'm in the car, and I don't really want to be the guy in the middle of it. Can I just describe it? It's, uh, basically a gray house with a blue door, on the corner.
I understand. It does make it hard for them to find without a street, though. Do you know the name of the street you're on, even if not the number?

[pause] Hang on, let me look. My phone's, uh, my charging cable only works at one angle so the screen keeps dying on me, basically I have to hold it just right. Okay, it's back. I'll be honest, I'm worried they won't come if I don't give anything.

No, that's fine, take your time. Here's what I can do. I'll take down what you've told me, the dog's description and the gray house with the blue door, and I can take your number so the officer can call you for the exact spot.
Yeah, okay. That works. It's 401-555-0190.
Four zero one, five five five, zero one nine zero. And your name?
Joel Varela. V-A-R-E-L-A.

Thank you, Mr. Varela. Now, our office isn't the one that dispatches, so I'm going to send this over to animal control right away and mark it as a dog outside in the rain and cold. Is the dog able to move around, or does it seem hurt?
It's moving. It's walking back and forth, kind of pulling at the rope. I don't think it's hurt, it just looks miserable. I just keep thinking it's going to get way colder tonight.
That's a fair concern. If you see it get worse, like it stops moving or collapses, call the police non-emergency line right away, because that's urgent.
Okay. Yeah, I will. And can you tell me roughly how long before somebody shows up? Basically I just want to know if I should stay here.

I can't give you a time, because it depends on where the officer is. Rainy days are busy. But it'll go in as soon as we hang up. You don't need to stay if you have to get back to work, as long as the officer has your number.
Okay. Alright. I'll probably stay a few more minutes anyway. Thanks, Owen. I appreciate you taking it seriously.
Of course. Take care, Mr. Varela, and stay dry.
You too. Bye.
